units.translation: May a plague of men never empty this city (thus Hermann for 'of these')
'with the remaining' in a corrupt passage.
hearing the rest of my words
let the rest of the contests be learned from you
if you can say what remains of the toils
until you learn the rest as well
to know the remaining grief beforehand
when you learn the remaining evils
or will you tell of some remaining misery here?
if you have anything remaining or omitted to tell here
the rest I will tell to you and to her in common
and all who remained and happened to be saved
do you see this remnant of my dress?
for us, the remaining of the Argive army
see the remaining affairs of the Atreidae in a helpless state
where then are the remaining oracles of Loxias?
and for the future this council of judges will always be for the army of Aegeus
having sworn for the future for all time
so that this company of the land may be gracious and in the future be distinguished by good fortune in men
for the rest I will keep a faithful day-watchman eye
for the future, if anything better should befall
this advice I have extended to my citizens for the future
having been harmed in the last courses
this is my task, to decide the final judgment
persuaded by the oracles of Loxias
why do you lament these things about Loxias?
or did Loxias also proclaim it?
Loxias is the prophet of father Zeus
let it be a care to mighty Loxias himself
I have come at the commands of Loxias
and Loxias is jointly responsible for these things
by the grace of Pallas and Loxias
for father Zeus sends these oracles to Loxias

Aeschylus would seem to call the baths 'louteria' (fr. 332): 'but from the greatest baths easily.' The verse that precedes in Pollux, 'he washes indeed in the bath a second time,' was rightly bracketed by Bekker: for it belongs to the preceding word 'bath' in Pollux. Whether it is Aeschylus's or another poet's is uncertain.
slain in the bath, the warlord of the Achaeans perished
The example fr. 332 is uncertain, about which see under the word λουτήριον.
having cleansed her husband who shared her bed with baths
remember the baths in which you were slain
and warm baths and a bed that charms away toils
having hidden with embroidered nets, which bore witness to the murder in the baths
